turns.content: A point charge q follows a trajectory s(t). Its field is observed at position r and time t, while the relevant source event occurs at an earlier time t_r satisfying t-t_r=d/c, where d_vector=r-s(t_r) and d=|d_vector|. What potential framework is appropriate, and how do the geometry and time delay enter it?
Contrast the retarded solution with an advanced solution and identify which boundary condition is compatible with a field generated at the earlier time t_r.
Let n=d_vector/d and let v be the charge velocity at t_r. Explain how the retarded-time Jacobian produces the factor 1-n dot v/c, including the sign of the velocity term.
Using that factor, write the Lienard-Wiechert scalar potential V(r,t) in terms of q, epsilon_0, d, n, v, and c, with every source quantity evaluated at t_r.
Rewrite the scalar potential using d_vector directly so that its denominator contains dc-d_vector dot v.
Starting from the standard Lienard-Wiechert relation between the vector and scalar potentials, and using mu_0 epsilon_0=1/c^2, express the vector potential in the same d-vector notation.
State both potentials together, with all constants, the common denominator, and the retarded-time evaluation made explicit.
Check the static limit v=0. What do V and A reduce to, and what does that check show about the sign and normalization?
Give the final retarded scalar and vector potentials and explain the geometric meaning of their denominator.
